title: Cramer’s rule and a selected unknown

exposition.text:
For an invertible n × n matrix A and system Ax = b, replace column j of A by b to obtain A .

question.text:
The system x + 2y + z = 0, 2x + y − z = 3, x − y + 2z = 1 has a unique solution. What is y?
1 1 1 2
(A) − (B) − (C) 0 (D) (E)
2 3 3 3

solution.text:
T
The coefficient determinant is −12. Replacing column two by (0, 3, 1) gives determinant 6,
so y = 6/(−12) = −1/2. Direct substitution gives (x, y, z) = (3/2, −1/2, −1/2).

question.text:
An invertible matrix A has columns c , c , c . A new matrix has columns c , 2c − 3c + 4c , c .
1 2 3 1 1 2 3 3
What is the ratio of its determinant to det A?
(A) −4 (B) −3 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 4

solution.text:
By multilinearity only the −3c term in the second column contributes; the other terms
2
duplicate another column and have zero determinant. The ratio is −3, matching the second
coordinate in Cramer notation.

question.text:
T
Let A = diag(1, 0, 0) and b = (0, 1, 0) . If A replaces column j of A by b, which statement is
j
correct?
(A) All three det A vanish, and Ax = b is inconsistent.
j
(B) All three det A vanish, and Ax = b has infinitely many solutions.
j
(C) Exactly one det A is nonzero, and the system is inconsistent.
j
(D) Exactly one det A is nonzero, and the system has a unique solution.
j
(E) All three det A are nonzero.
j

solution.text:
Every replacement matrix still has a zero column, so all three numerators vanish. Yet
every vector Ax has second coordinate zero, whereas b has second coordinate one. Thus the
system is inconsistent despite every formal Cramer numerator being zero; division by the
zero determinant supplies no solution criterion.

question.text:
An invertible 3 × 3 matrix A has columns c , c , c , and Ax = b. The matrix with columns

(A) 3 (B) 4 (C) 6 (D) 7 (E) 8

solution.text:
Multilinearity leaves the original determinant and three single-column replacements. Every
term containing two copies of b vanishes. Cramer gives the total as (1 + x + x + x ) det A.

Dividing by the nonzero determinant yields the sum six.
